title: An immersion of a syntomic scheme into a smooth scheme over the base is a regular immersion

standard_prerequisites.name: A syntomic morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, and a smooth morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, cited from the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the hypotheses of the fibrewise criterion for a relative quasi-regular immersion.

standard_prerequisites.name: The fibrewise criterion producing a relative quasi-regular immersion from a closed subscheme whose fibres are quasi-regular, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the claim to the statement that each fibre is a quasi-regular closed subscheme.

standard_prerequisites.name: Over a locally Noetherian scheme regularity of an immersion can be checked at points, cited from the same chapter, and a finite type scheme over a field is Noetherian
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the fibre statement to be checked at individual points.

standard_prerequisites.name: The local ring of a point of a fibre of a syntomic morphism is a local complete intersection over the residue field of the base point, the local ring of a point of a smooth scheme over a field is regular, and a quotient of a regular local ring by an ideal defining a local complete intersection is cut out by a regular sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the pointwise algebra input that closes the argument.

core_obligations: Reduce to a closed immersion: replacing the smooth scheme by an open neighbourhood of the image one may assume the given immersion is a closed immersion (proof lines 5686-5688).

Set up the fibrewise criterion: the closed subscheme is syntomic hence flat and locally of finite presentation over the base, the ambient scheme is smooth hence flat and locally of finite presentation, so by the fibrewise criterion it is enough to show that each fibre of the closed subscheme in the corresponding fibre of the smooth morphism is a quasi-regular closed subscheme (proof lines 5689-5694).

Check the fibres at points: each fibre of a smooth morphism over a field is locally of finite type hence Noetherian, so quasi-regularity of the closed subscheme can be checked at points, and at a point the local ring of the small scheme is a local complete intersection over the residue field while the local ring of the ambient fibre is regular, so the kernel of the surjection between them is generated by a regular sequence (proof lines 5695-5717).
proof_roadmap: Make the immersion closed and reduce to the fibrewise criterion for relative quasi-regular immersions (proof lines 5686-5694).
Verify the criterion pointwise on the fibres, where a local complete intersection quotient of a regular local ring is cut out by a regular sequence (proof lines 5695-5717).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that in a commutative triangle with a syntomic morphism into a smooth morphism over the same base, the immersion involved is a regular immersion (statement lines 5672-5684). The counted proof reduces the statement to a closed immersion, applies the fibrewise criterion for relative quasi-regular immersions to reduce to the fibres, and then checks the fibres pointwise, where the local ring of the fibre of the syntomic morphism is a local complete intersection over the residue field while the local ring of the fibre of the smooth morphism is regular, so the defining ideal is generated by a regular sequence (proof lines 5686-5717). It is H2: every step is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are standard flatness and local complete intersection statements.
